name: Hesper Quillon
cause: hanged for the murder of her master
summary: Cook to the Margrave of Dunmere for twenty years. Poisoned his supper on the eve of his burning three villages for unpaid tithe. The household's taster, a page aged twelve, died with him.

entries.text: Poisoned the Margrave of Dunmere at his own table.
Caused the death of the page Lutz, taster to the household ("unintended").
The burnings were never carried out; some four hundred villagers were spared.
Fed beggars at the kitchen door for twenty years, against orders.
Confessed at once so the kitchen staff would not be put to the question.

hidden.text: Lied to this tribunal about the boy.

archive.title: Dunmere kitchen roster
cards: Tasting rota, week of the tithe court, in the cook's own hand.
Taster: Lutz, page, aged 12. Struck through: Brandt, taster thirty years.
Beside Brandt: 'to the stables, by order of Cook.'

fact.text: She wrote the tasting rota herself and put the boy on it.
She told this tribunal she did not know. She wrote the rota.

answer: Because he'd have done it. He'd burnt Asher's Ford the year before and laughed at supper.
I had the pot and nobody else had anything.
questions.card: He'd burnt Asher's Ford the year before. She had the pot.

fact.text: The Margrave had burned Asher's Ford the year before; the threat was real.

questions.text: Did you know the boy would taste it?
answer: No. It should have been old Brandt. God's teeth, do you think I'd have... no. I did not know.
questions.card: Says it should have been old Brandt. Denies knowing.

answer: ...Brandt had tasted for him thirty years and could smell a bad egg through a wall. Lutz couldn't.
If Brandt tasted, the Margrave lived and three villages burned.
I weighed a boy against four hundred. I'd like to tell you it was hard.
questions.card: Put Lutz on the rota because Brandt would have smelled it. Weighed him.

fact.text: She weighed one boy against four hundred villagers, and says so plainly.

heaven: Lutz, admitted long ago, is asked whether he objects. He asks whether the villages are still there.
Told yes, he says he would like to think about it.
hell: The Wardens log one debt, owed to Lutz.
The Margrave, already in their keeping, is told his cook has arrived, and is reported to be unsettled.

ext.mitigating: No lawful remedy existed against the Margrave; she acted alone and accepted the rope to shield others.
ext.note: C31 resolved in data: q3 requires q2 asked, so the lie (h1) only exists if she told it; G is computed on the full -1 record.
